subject: Finai POC: canary variant fallback + temporary concurrency exemption
messages:
From: Maya Kapoor <maya@finai.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Canary variant fallback behavior + request for temporary concurrency bump

Hey Logan,

Quick note from our POC run this morning — during a canary rollout we hit an unusual pattern where some user requests were routed to a lower-capacity variant and we saw ~3x latency for a subset of short-chat requests. We captured a small set of logs and a timing trace (attached).

Two asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether the platform will automatically fall back to the full-capacity variant when latency crosses the threshold, or whether we need to configure an explicit routing policy?
- Our ops team asked whether Redwood can temporarily increase allowed concurrency for the canary to reduce that skew while we finish validation. This is blocking the next demo next week.

Thanks — appreciate any clarity you can provide.

— Maya
Director of Product, Finai Health

Attachments: finai-prod-sample-logs-20270523.zip
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Platform Runtime <runtime-team@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Canary variant fallback behavior + request for temporary concurrency bump

Forwarding Finai's note and logs. Short summary of asks:
- Confirm fallback semantics for variant routing under load.
- Can we grant a temporary concurrency exemption for Finai's canary while they finish validation (they're on a POC plan, deal FIN-6021)?

Context: Finai is demoing to a payer partner next Wednesday; they saw a subset of short requests routed to a quantized/low-capacity variant that spikes p50/p95. They want either auto-fallback or a manual lift.

What I need from runtime:
1) Quick explanation of how the smart routing chooses variants when capacity is constrained (policy precedence, thresholds).
2) Practical mitigation we can apply today (config change, temp quota bump, or a routing rule).
3) If an exemption is required, how long will it take to apply and are there any cost/regression risks?

Soojin / Karthik — can you triage? If we need an exception sign-off, I can take it to CS/Revenue ops.

Thanks,
Logan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Canary variant fallback behavior + request for temporary concurrency bump

Logan — took a look at the attached traces. High-level: the routing layer prefers lower-cost variants when they report available capacity. In this case we saw a small mismatch in the sequence-length distribution estimation that made the route score favor the quantized variant for short inputs, and that variant is currently configured with a low concurrency cap for the canary.

Options (practical, ranked):
- Immediate: add a routing override for Finai's canary route to pin to the primary variant for 24–72 hours. Low risk, quick (config change, <2 hours).
- Immediate alternative: increase concurrency cap on the quantized variant for the canary pool (possible but raises cost and some tail latency risk).
- Short-term roadmap: improve the route scoring heuristic to include measured p95 penalties for variant mismatch (will require a small change to the scoring service, ETA 2–3 sprints).

If Finai wants a fast unblock for the demo, I'd recommend the routing override. Marcus can apply the config change if you get sign-off from Sales/CS on the exemption window.

Notes: we should log the exemption in JIRA-INF-1247 so we don't leave it open. Also recommend adding a small automated smoke test to the POC harness to surface this earlier.

— Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Kapoor <maya@finai.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Canary variant fallback behavior + request for temporary concurrency bump

Maya — quick update and plan:

- We can apply a routing override to keep Finai's canary pinned to the primary variant for the next 72 hours. That will prevent the low-capacity variant from being chosen while you finish validation. Marcus will apply the change once we get your confirmation.
- We've logged the follow-up engineering work to reduce variant-scoring regressions (JIRA-INF-1247) and will prioritize a smoke test in the POC harness.

Please reply with a short OK if you want us to apply the 72-hour override. If you'd rather the concurrency bump on the quantized variant instead, tell us and we'll outline expected cost delta.

Thanks — aiming to keep your demo on track.

Best,
